notYet: Not yet part of Plato's Mediterranean

stages.name: Independent peoples and kingdoms
stages.desc: Illyrians, Thracians, Paeonians, and Egypt under its own pharaohs

stages.name: Greek city-states
stages.desc: Free Greek cities, ruling themselves or led by Sparta, Athens or Thebes

stages.name: Persian Empire
stages.desc: Provinces of the Great King, from Anatolia to the Levant

stages.name: Carthage
stages.desc: The Phoenician city of North Africa and its western Mediterranean domain

stages.name: Syracuse's tyrants
stages.desc: Dionysius the First and his son, masters of Sicily and the Greek south

stages.name: War and revolt
stages.desc: Regions torn by great wars, invasions and rebellions

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Greek and Phoenician kingdoms of Cyprus under Persian rule
Evagoras, king of Salamis, wages a long war against Persia
Evagoras submits and keeps Salamis as a vassal king

states.name: Israel
timeline: The coast and Judah, Persian provinces of Beyond the River

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Judah and Samaria, Persian provinces of Beyond the River

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Sidon, Tyre and the Phoenician cities, whose fleets serve the Persian king

states.name: Syria
timeline: The Persian province Beyond the River, with Phoenician Arwad on its coast

states.name: North Macedonia
timeline: The Paeonians and other upland peoples north of Macedon
Philip the Second of Macedon defeats the Paeonians and Illyrians

states.name: Albania
timeline: Illyrian peoples; Greek colonies at Epidamnus and Apollonia on the coast
Dionysius of Syracuse founds Lissus and backs Illyrian allies on the Adriatic

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Persian provinces of Anatolia; the Greek cities of the coast belong to Athens' empire
The King's Peace hands the Greek cities of Asia to Persia
The Great Satraps' Revolt shakes western Anatolia (c. 366–360)
The revolt collapses and Persian rule is restored

states.name: Libya
timeline: Cyrene and the Greek cities of Cyrenaica; Libyan peoples inland, Carthaginian posts to the west
By a doubtful tradition, Plato visits the mathematician Theodorus at Cyrene

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage, the great Phoenician city of the west
Carthage begins its long wars against the Greeks of Sicily

states.name: Greece
timeline: Athens and Sparta are at war; Plato is born in Athens (some said Aegina) around 428
Athens surrenders; Sparta dominates Greece and the Thirty rule Athens for a year
Athens' restored democracy tries and executes Socrates
The Corinthian War: Athens, Thebes, Corinth and Argos against Sparta
The King's Peace, dictated by Persia, ends the war; Plato opens the Academy
Thebes breaks Sparta's power at Leuctra; years of war follow
After the drawn battle of Mantinea, a general peace; no city leads Greece
The Third Sacred War over Delphi; Philip of Macedon advances from the north
Philip destroys Olynthus; Plato dies in Athens

states.name: Italy
timeline: Free Greek cities of Sicily and the south (Syracuse, Acragas, Taras, Croton); Italic peoples, Etruscans and Rome further north
Athens' great armada besieges Syracuse; it is destroyed in 413
Syracuse is victorious and free
Carthage invades Sicily and destroys Selinus, Himera and then Acragas
Dionysius the First seizes power in Syracuse; he will rule for thirty-eight years
Plato's first visit, at about forty; he meets the young Dion
Dionysius the First dies; his son succeeds; Plato's second visit
Plato's third visit ends in near-captivity
Dion sails from Greece with about eight hundred mercenaries and takes Syracuse
Dion is murdered by Callippus; Syracuse falls into faction and mercenary rule

states.name: Bulgaria
timeline: The Odrysian kingdom of Thrace

states.name: Egypt
timeline: A province of the Persian Empire
Egypt breaks free of Persia under its own pharaohs, beginning with Amyrtaeus
Plato is said to study with the priests of Heliopolis (a late tradition)
A Persian invasion of the Nile delta fails
Nectanebo the Second, Egypt's last native pharaoh, takes the throne

states.name: N. Cyprus
timeline: Greek and Phoenician kingdoms of Cyprus under Persian rule
Evagoras, king of Salamis, wages a long war against Persia
Evagoras submits and keeps Salamis as a vassal king

states.name: Malta
timeline: Phoenician harbours and sanctuaries within Carthage's sphere

events.title: Plato is born
events.text: Aristocles, later called Plato, is born to Ariston and Perictione around 428/7; some said on Aegina.

events.title: Armada for Sicily
events.text: Athens' great fleet sails from Piraeus to conquer Syracuse; two years later it is destroyed.

events.title: Carthage invades Sicily
events.text: A Carthaginian army destroys the Greek cities of Selinus and Himera.

events.title: Meets Socrates
events.text: By tradition, Plato hears Socrates at about twenty and burns the tragedies he had written.

events.title: Dionysius seizes power
events.text: A young officer makes himself tyrant of Syracuse during the war with Carthage.

events.title: The Thirty
events.text: Athens surrenders; Critias, Plato's mother's cousin, leads the junta and invites Plato to join.

events.title: Egypt breaks free
events.text: Amyrtaeus of Sais leads Egypt out of the Persian Empire.

events.title: Death of Socrates
events.text: The restored democracy condemns Socrates for impiety; Plato is at the trial but ill on the last day.

events.title: Refuge at Megara
events.text: Plato, about twenty-eight, withdraws to the philosopher Euclides with other friends of Socrates.

events.title: Corinthian War
events.text: Athens, Thebes, Corinth and Argos take up arms against Sparta.

events.title: Theodorus at Cyrene
events.text: Later writers say Plato studied with the mathematician Theodorus here; a doubtful tradition.

events.title: Evagoras' war
events.text: The king of Salamis on Cyprus begins a ten-year war against Persia.

events.title: The priests of Egypt
events.text: Strabo was shown 'Plato's house' at Heliopolis; the visit is a late and doubtful tradition.

events.title: Archytas of Taras
events.text: In southern Italy Plato meets the Pythagoreans and Archytas, philosopher, mathematician and general.

events.title: First voyage
events.text: Plato, about forty, reaches Syracuse, dislikes the court's luxury and befriends the young Dion.

events.title: Sold at Aegina?
events.text: A later legend: the angry tyrant has Plato sold as a slave here, until Anniceris of Cyrene ransoms him.

events.title: The King's Peace
events.text: Persia dictates peace to the Greeks and takes the Greek cities of Asia.

events.title: The Academy
events.text: Plato begins teaching in the grove of the hero Akademos, outside the walls of Athens.

events.title: Lissus
events.text: Dionysius of Syracuse plants a colony on the Adriatic and arms Illyrian allies.

events.title: The Republic
events.text: Plato's dialogue on justice, with the cave and the philosopher-kings, is usually dated to around now.

events.title: Persia fails in the delta
events.text: A Persian and Greek mercenary invasion of Egypt is beaten back from the Nile.

events.title: Leuctra
events.text: Thebes defeats Sparta in open battle; Spartan supremacy in Greece is over.

events.title: Aristotle arrives
events.text: A seventeen-year-old from Stagira joins the Academy and stays twenty years.

events.title: Second voyage
events.text: Dionysius the First dies; Dion calls Plato to teach the new tyrant, his son.

events.title: Dion exiled
events.text: About three months after Plato arrives, Dionysius the Second puts Dion on a small boat and drives him out.

events.title: Satraps' revolt
events.text: Persia's governors in Anatolia rise against the Great King (c. 366–360).

events.title: Mantinea
events.text: Thebes wins but loses its leader Epaminondas; no city now leads Greece.

events.title: Third voyage
events.text: Summoned again, Plato quarrels with Dionysius over Dion's estates and is lodged among hostile mercenaries.

events.title: Archytas sends a ship
events.text: Archytas sends envoys and a ship from Taras to bring Plato safely home.

events.title: Olympia
events.text: At the Olympic games, Plato meets the exiled Dion and tells him the story.

events.title: Nectanebo II
events.text: Egypt's last native pharaoh takes the throne at Sebennytos.

events.title: Philip in the north
events.text: Philip the Second of Macedon defeats the Paeonians and the Illyrians.

events.title: Dion sails
events.text: From Zacynthus, Dion sets out for Sicily with about eight hundred mercenaries.

events.title: Dion takes Syracuse
events.text: Dion enters the city while Dionysius the Second is away; the tyrant later flees.

events.title: Sacred War
events.text: Phocis seizes Delphi; a ten-year war draws in Thebes, Athens and Philip.

events.title: Dion murdered
events.text: Callippus, an Athenian who had studied at the Academy, has Dion killed at a festival.

events.title: The Laws
events.text: Plato's last and longest work sketches a second-best city ruled by laws, left unrevised at his death.

events.title: Olynthus destroyed
events.text: Philip of Macedon razes Olynthus and sells its people into slavery.

events.title: Death of Plato
events.text: Plato dies in Athens in 348/7, about eighty-one, and is buried in the Academy.

eras: The Thirty and the trial of Socrates
chartNote: Share of the area of the mapped countries, by the power that led each present-day country's territory. Regions are today's boundaries and often mixed: Italy is one region, coloured by Syracuse, the leading power of the Greek West, and Libya by Greek Cyrene. Egypt's size swings the shares. A simplification; dates are approximate turning points, and Plato's journeys to Cyrene and Egypt are traditions, not facts.
